concerns.text: The plan cites 'Fermi Science Support Center (FSSC)' and 'Fermi GBM Trigger Catalog' as the source for the 'top 30 brightest GRBs' but fails to provide a specific, programmatic URL or accession ID for the selection criteria. The research.md explicitly notes 'NO verified source found' for a direct URL. Without a canonical, programmatic link to the specific fluence-ranked list or the exact API endpoint used to derive the 'top 30', the dataset selection is non-reproducible and violates Constitution Principle I (Reproducibility) and Principle II (Verified Accuracy). The plan must cite the exact URL or API query string used to generate the list.

The research strategy relies on 'standard public access pattern' (e.g., `https://heasarc.gsfc.nasa.gov/FTP/fermi/data/gbm/`) but admits the 'top 30' list is not a static file. The plan assumes the code will 'query the FSSC API or download the full catalog and filter locally' without defining the specific API endpoint or the exact fluence metric (e.g., peak flux vs. total fluence, energy range for fluence calculation) used for ranking. This ambiguity makes the dataset definition 'top 30 brightest' non-deterministic and unverified against the primary source.
